passages.original: Aliter betacios varrones. Varro: ,,betacios sed nigros quorum detersas radices, ex mulso decoctos cum sale modico et oleo, vel sale qua et oleo in se cocto iusculum facere et potare". melius etiam, si in eo pullus sit decoctus.
passages.english: Varro's beets, another way. Varro [says]: "[Take] beets, but black ones, whose roots have been cleaned off; boil them in honeyed wine with a little salt and oil, or with salt, water and oil; make a broth cooked down in itself, and drink it." It is even better if a chicken has been boiled in it.
passages.notes: "sale qua et oleo" appears corrupt; read as "sale, aqua et oleo" (salt, water and oil). "betacios varrones" is taken as "beets à la Varro"; the sense of the title is uncertain. The construction of the quoted recipe is loose (infinitives "facere et potare"), and its syntax has been smoothed into instructions.
